── NESSA'S WEEK ──
Nessa is 41 and new to running, aiming to run the whole Corrowmore Harvest 5K on 15 November without walking. Nessa walk-runs three mornings a week (Monday, Wednesday and Saturday) and walks the dog most days.
Recent weeks: 7, 0, 5.1, 0 km
This week: 0 km over 0 runs. Missed 3 of 3 planned runs.
Body: "Fine, a bit stiff from all the driving."
Feeling: "Want to get going again."
Asks: "I haven't run for two weeks. Do I have to start again from the beginning? And is the 5K in four weeks still realistic?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Nessa: Welcome back, and sorry about the fortnight you've just had. …
Answers: (1) No, you do not start from the beginning. Two weeks off takes a little edge off your fitness, not all of it. (2) On the 5K being four weeks away: finishing it is realistic, and I would bet on you to do that well. …
Next week:
Mon: easy, walk-run 21 min, 7 x (2 min run and 1 min walk), conversational effort…
Tue: rest. Protects the comeback and keeps the legs fresh for Wednesday.
Wed: easy, walk-run 24 min, 8 x (2 min run and 1 min walk), same easy effort. Back to…
Thu: rest. A dog walk is lovely, no running.
Fri: rest. Sets up a good Saturday.
Sat: easy, walk-run 24 min, 6 x (3 min run and 1 min walk), still conversational. First…
Sun: rest. Lets this first week back settle before we lengthen again.
